chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, from Muawiya ibn Hakim, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When a man swears an oath of Zihar and then breaks it, the expiation is upon him before he copulates; and if the Zihar was from him without being an oath, then the expiation is upon him after he copulates.

key_terms.الظِّهَار: Zihar: A form of divorce in pre-Islamic and early Islamic law where a man likens his wife's back to his mother's back, prohibiting sexual relations until expiation is made.
key_terms.الكَفَّارَةُ: Kaffarah: The expiation or penalty required to atone for breaking an oath or performing Zihar.
key_terms.يُوَاقِعَ: Yuwaqi': To copulate or consummate the marriage.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in expiation timing for Zihar when sworn as an oath versus declared without an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural timing of Kaffarah (expiation) for Zihar based on whether the declaration was coupled with an oath (Yamin) or made as a standalone statement. It reflects the Shia juristic distinction that an oath-bound Zihar acts as a conditional barrier requiring expiation prior to consummation, whereas a non-oath Zihar is rectified after the act, highlighting the legal weight of the verbal formula used.
